requirements: Reproduce the core contributions of FSE-DP: a multi-chiplet parallelization strategy with micro-slice expert streaming, virtualization rules, and a dynamic expert-trajectory scheduler for low-batch MoE inference.

sub_tasks.requirements: The multi-chiplet simulation/emulation environment used for evaluation is set up, including the cycle-accurate simulator, RTL-synthesized scheduler, and hardware specifications (5nm test chip, UCIe D2D IPs, DDR3-1600, PE array, NLU, DMU).
The per-chiplet compute die architecture and its specifications are implemented, matching the 5nm test chip parameters.
Code has been implemented that models a compute die containing a PE array, non-linear unit (NLU), UCIe D2D IP module(s), and a data movement unit (DMU) for data transfer and format conversion.

verification.spec: Import the compute-die model class from the codebase and verify by attribute or submodule inspection that it exposes distinct components for: PE array (with configurable MAC count), non-linear unit (NLU), UCIe D2D IP interface, and a DMU for data transfer/format conversion. Each component must be individually instantiable and referenced in the die's forward/simulate method.

sub_tasks.requirements: The PE array is configured with 2048 MAC units per compute die operating at 800 MHz, yielding the reported per-die peak throughput of 4.865 TOPS.

verification.spec: Inspect the simulator/accelerator configuration file for each compute die. Assert that num_mac_units == 2048, clock_frequency == 800e6 Hz, and derived peak throughput is approximately 4.865 TOPS (2 * 2048 * 800e6 = 3.28 TOPS integer; check the configured value matches Table I).

sub_tasks.requirements: The compute die footprint is set to 2.69mm x 4.72mm, consistent with the Samsung 5nm 1P13M CMOS test chip specification, and area/power constraints (die area limit and package power limit used in DSE) reflect this baseline.

verification.spec: Inspect the compute-die configuration used by the simulator/DSE. Verify the die dimensions equal 2.69mm x 4.72mm (area ~12.7 mm^2) and that the DSE constraint file specifies a per-die area limit and package power limit consistent with the 5nm test-chip baseline reported in Table I.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each chiplet includes a router that receives task sequences from the scheduler, holds static instruction sequences for transformer operations, and generates its communication routing table at runtime based on the trajectory provided by the scheduler.

verification.spec: In the chiplet model, verify (1) it exposes a router component that accepts task sequences pushed by the scheduler API; (2) it stores a static instruction sequence for transformer ops accessible before runtime; and (3) given a scheduler-provided trajectory, the router constructs its routing table at runtime (call get_routing_table() before and after supplying a new trajectory and confirm the table changes).

sub_tasks.requirements: The inter-chiplet and off-chip memory subsystem models are implemented, capturing UCIe D2D interconnect and DDR3 characteristics.

Code has been implemented that models UCIe-compliant D2D IPs between chiplets with an aggregate per-link bandwidth of 288 GB/s, per-pin data rates in the 4-24 Gbps range, and an FDI-to-FDI latency of 4.02 ns.

verification.spec: Inspect the D2D interconnect configuration in the simulator. Assert that per-link aggregate bandwidth equals 288 GB/s, per-pin data rate is configurable within 4-24 Gbps, and FDI-to-FDI latency is set to 4.02 ns.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Network-on-Package is modelled as a 2D-mesh interconnect capable of applying multiple ring trajectories concurrently for arrays larger than 2x2.

verification.spec: Instantiate the NoP as a 2D-mesh topology with dimensions >2x2 (e.g., 3x3 and 4x4). Submit a workload requiring at least two concurrent expert trajectories and verify by inspecting the routing state that multiple non-overlapping ring trajectories are scheduled and executed simultaneously without conflict.

sub_tasks.requirements: The DDR memory subsystem is modelled as DDR3-1600 with four channels providing 4 x 25.6 GB/s of aggregate bandwidth at 800 MHz, driving off-chip expert weight loading traffic.

verification.spec: Inspect DDR configuration in the simulator. Assert num_channels == 4, per_channel_bandwidth == 25.6 GB/s, aggregate_bandwidth == 102.4 GB/s, memory_type == 'DDR3-1600', and clock_frequency == 800 MHz.

sub_tasks.requirements: The simulator correctly accounts for D2D transfer time along the chosen expert trajectories so that additional inter-chiplet hops manifest as idle cycles impacting utilization at larger array scales.

verification.spec: Simulate the same workload on a 2x2 and a 4x4 array using the same per-link D2D bandwidth. Verify that D2D transfer latency is a modeled component in the timing trace (nonzero cycles booked for each hop) and that increasing array size (with correspondingly longer trajectories) results in higher recorded idle cycles due to D2D transit, reducing utilization at the larger scale.

sub_tasks.requirements: The 2x2 chiplet prototype floorplan and package integration used for evaluation (Figure 10) are reproduced or represented in the simulation environment.

The evaluation environment instantiates a 2x2 chiplet package matching the taped-out test chip's floorplan (four compute dies plus an I/O die that hosts the scheduler) with the specified per-die area and D2D placement.

verification.spec: Load the default evaluation configuration and verify: 4 compute dies plus 1 I/O die are instantiated; each compute die has the specified 2.69x4.72 mm area; the I/O die hosts the scheduler module; and D2D links are placed matching the taped-out chip floorplan (adjacency graph of the four dies is a 2x2 mesh with the I/O die connecting to all four).

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler is placed in the I/O die in the simulated system such that expert-information lookup, idle-chiplet tracking, and expert-chiplet matching all execute off the compute dies, matching the described hardware partitioning.

verification.spec: Inspect the simulated system topology and verify the scheduler module (EIT, ICV, E-C Matcher) is instantiated as a component of the I/O die object, not any of the compute-die objects. Also confirm scheduling-related SRAM/logic area is charged to the I/O die's area budget rather than the compute dies.

sub_tasks.requirements: The environment supports extending the simulated array beyond 2x2 (to 3x3 and 4x4 chiplet arrays) with the same per-die and per-link specifications, enabling scalability experiments.

verification.spec: Instantiate the simulator with array shapes {2x2, 3x3, 4x4}, using the same per-die spec (800 MHz, PE array size, buffer sizes) and same per-link D2D bandwidth. Run a representative MoE forward pass on each array and verify the simulator completes and produces valid utilization/latency reports for all three shapes.

sub_tasks.requirements: The four MoE models (Phi-3.5-MoE, Yuan2.0-M32, DeepSeek-MoE, Qwen3-30B-A3B) and the evaluation datasets (Wikitext-2, C4, WinoGrande) are available with correct configurations.
MoE model configurations are correctly acquired and loaded.

verification.spec: Load the Phi-3.5-MoE model configuration and assert num_experts_per_layer == 16, top_k == 2, hidden_size == 4096, ffn_intermediate_size == 3200, num_attention_heads == 32, and total parameter count is approximately 41.9B (within 5%).

verification.spec: Load the Yuan2.0-M32 model configuration and assert num_experts_per_layer == 32, top_k == 2, hidden_size == 2048, ffn_intermediate_size == 4096, num_attention_heads == 16, and total parameter count is approximately 40B (within 5%).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the DeepSeek-MoE-16B model configuration with 64 experts per layer, 6+2 active experts (6 routed + 2 shared), Dmodel=2048, Dffn=1408, 16 attention heads, and ~16.4B parameters, matching Table I.

verification.spec: Load the DeepSeek-MoE-16B model configuration and assert num_routed_experts == 64, num_active_routed == 6, num_shared_experts == 2, hidden_size == 2048, ffn_intermediate_size == 1408, num_attention_heads == 16, and total parameter count is approximately 16.4B (within 5%).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the Qwen3-30B-A3B model configuration with 128 experts per layer, 8 active experts, Dmodel=2048, Dffn=768 (per expert), 32 attention heads, and ~30B parameters, matching Table I.

verification.spec: Load the Qwen3-30B-A3B model configuration and assert num_experts_per_layer == 128, top_k == 8, hidden_size == 2048, per_expert_intermediate_size == 768, num_attention_heads == 32, and total parameter count is approximately 30B (within 5%).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to expose per-model expert dimension parameters (DExpert) consistent with Figure 2(a), enabling downstream simulation to compute per-expert MAC and memory footprints correctly across all four models.

verification.spec: Query the model-config API for all four supported models and verify DExpert equals the values in Figure 2(a): DeepSeek-MoE=1408, Qwen3-30B-A3B=768, DeepSeek-V2/V3=2048, OLMoE=1024, Qwen1.5-MoE=1408, Phi-3.5-MoE per its spec. Also verify DFFN and DModel fields are present and used by the simulator to compute per-expert MAC and memory footprints.

sub_tasks.requirements: Evaluation datasets are acquired and prepared for tokenization and inference.
Code has been implemented to acquire the Wikitext-2 language modeling dataset and expose it as a tokenizable stream of text usable for MoE forward-pass evaluation.

verification.spec: Call the dataset-loading API for Wikitext-2 and verify it returns a stream/iterable of text records. Feed the stream through a tokenizer (e.g., the Qwen3 tokenizer) and confirm at least 1000 tokens can be produced without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to acquire the C4 dataset and expose it as a tokenizable stream of text usable for MoE forward-pass evaluation.

verification.spec: Call the dataset-loading API for C4 (validation or streaming split) and verify it returns a stream/iterable of text records. Feed the stream through a tokenizer and confirm at least 1000 tokens are produced without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to acquire the WinoGrande dataset for use in the motivational long-tail expert activation profiling (Section II / Figure 2).

verification.spec: Call the dataset-loading API for WinoGrande and verify it returns iterable examples suitable for tokenization. Confirm the returned examples contain the fields needed to run MoE gating profiling as described in Section II.

sub_tasks.requirements: Request sampling and tokens-per-iteration input construction is implemented for evaluation.
Code has been implemented to sample requests from Wikitext-2 and C4 and aggregate their input tokens into a single forward-pass iteration with a configurable tokens-per-iteration (micro-batch) value.

verification.spec: Invoke the iteration-sampler with tokens_per_iteration=16, 64, 256, 1024 on Wikitext-2 and C4 sources. Verify the returned batch contains exactly the requested number of tokens aggregated from multiple sampled requests, and that per-request provenance metadata is preserved (so the same test can drive chunked-prefill mixing).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to support the four fixed tokens-per-iteration configurations (16, 64, 256, and 1024) used throughout the evaluation.

verification.spec: Inspect the evaluation harness and assert that the tokens-per-iteration parameter accepts and is exercised with each of the values {16, 64, 256, 1024}, and that each configuration successfully runs one MoE layer end-to-end.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to mix prefill and decode contexts from multiple concurrent requests within a single iteration (chunked-prefill-style aggregation) so that the effective batch reflects low-batch on-device conditions.

verification.spec: Configure the iteration builder to accept a mix of concurrent requests where some are in prefill and others in decode phase, and produce a single iteration containing tokens from both. Verify the resulting iteration contains tokens tagged as prefill and tokens tagged as decode from at least two different requests within the total tokens-per-iteration budget, matching the chunked-prefill setting described in Section III.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware scheduler (EIT, ICV, E-C Matcher, bitonic sorter) is implemented in RTL and synthesizes to the reported area (0.43 mm^2 in UMC 28nm) with sub-microsecond latency.
The top-level scheduler RTL module is implemented, integrating the EIT, ICV, E-C Matcher, bitonic sorter, token buffering router, and idle-chiplet reloader as specified in Figure 8.

Code has been implemented for a top-level scheduler RTL module (e.g., Verilog/SystemVerilog/Chisel) that instantiates the four subcomponents (EIT, ICV, E-C Matcher, bitonic sorter) and exposes an interface to receive gating outputs and emit per-expert trajectory/chiplet assignments.

verification.spec: Elaborate the top-level scheduler RTL module in a simulator (Verilator/Icarus) and check that it instantiates EIT, ICV, E-C Matcher, and a bitonic sorter, and exposes ports for gating-output input and per-expert (trajectory, chiplet) assignment output.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the scheduler is placed in the IO die of the multi-chiplet system and communicates task sequences to per-chiplet routers as described in Section V-B/V-C.

verification.spec: Inspect the multi-chiplet system's top-level integration file and confirm the scheduler RTL is instantiated inside the IO die module, with wired output channels to per-chiplet router interfaces.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Expert Information Table (EIT) is implemented as a single-cycle SRAM-based lookup mapping expert IDs to trajectory masks and activating-token counts.
Code has been implemented for an EIT RTL block that uses expert IDs as keys and stores, per entry, a relative trajectory descriptor and the number of tokens activating that expert.

verification.spec: Inspect the EIT RTL block and confirm the memory is keyed by expert ID and each entry stores fields for a relative trajectory descriptor and the token-activation count.

sub_tasks.requirements: The EIT performs lookups in a single clock cycle in simulation of the RTL, returning trajectory and token-count fields without iterative search.

verification.spec: Simulate the EIT RTL with a testbench that asserts an expert ID on the address port on cycle N and samples the data port on cycle N+1; verify trajectory and token-count fields are valid within a single clock cycle with no iterative search.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Idle Chiplet Vector (ICV) is implemented as an N-bit register bank supporting bitwise allocation and release updates.

Code has been implemented for the ICV as an N-bit register bank (N equals the number of chiplets) that supports concurrent reads for scheduling decisions and asynchronous writes on expert-completion events.

verification.spec: Inspect the RTL source for the Idle Chiplet Vector (ICV) module and confirm it is implemented as an N-bit register bank parameterized by the number of chiplets, with a read port usable each cycle by the scheduler and a separate asynchronous write port driven by expert-completion events. Elaborate the module in a simulator (e.g., Verilator/Icarus) and confirm reads and writes can occur concurrently without conflict.

sub_tasks.requirements: The ICV allocation path uses AND-NOT masking with the expert trajectory pattern to clear idle bits, and the release path uses OR with a completion mask to set idle bits, as described in Section V-B.

verification.spec: Instantiate the ICV RTL module in a testbench. Preload it with a known idle mask, then apply an allocation transaction with a trajectory pattern and check the next-cycle ICV equals (old_ICV AND NOT trajectory). Then apply a completion event with a completion mask and check the ICV equals (previous_ICV OR completion_mask).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Expert-Chiplet (E-C) Matcher is implemented to select computing chiplets and communication paths based on the ICV and per-expert trajectory.

Code has been implemented for the E-C Matcher RTL block that consumes an expert trajectory from the EIT and the current ICV, and outputs the assigned chiplet(s) and next-hop route for the expert's micro-slice streaming.

verification.spec: Locate the E-C Matcher RTL block, verify by code review that it has input ports for an expert trajectory from the EIT and the current ICV, and output ports for assigned chiplet IDs and next-hop route. Elaborate it and confirm the module compiles and produces outputs when driven with sample stimulus.

sub_tasks.requirements: The E-C Matcher only assigns an expert when its trajectory intersects the idle-chiplet set (T_e ∩ C_idle ≠ ∅), implementing the gating condition of Algorithm 1 line 6.

verification.spec: Testbench the E-C Matcher with two scenarios: (1) an expert trajectory that has non-empty intersection with the ICV idle set — check that the block issues a valid assignment; (2) an expert trajectory disjoint from the current ICV idle set — check that no assignment is issued (the expert is not scheduled).

sub_tasks.requirements: A bitonic sorter is implemented in RTL to sort experts by their token-activation counts in parallel, enabling hot/cold classification and paired-load ordering.
Code has been implemented for a parallel bitonic sorter that accepts the per-expert token counts read from the EIT and produces an ordered list of expert IDs by descending token count.

verification.spec: Instantiate the bitonic sorter RTL module. Drive it with vectors of (expert_id, token_count) pairs read from an EIT stub, and verify the output is the input expert IDs re-ordered by descending token count for several random and adversarial input vectors.

sub_tasks.requirements: The bitonic sorter output is consumed by a pairing stage that pairs experts from opposite ends of the sorted list (hot with cold), producing the ordered pair sequence E_sorted used by Algorithm 1.

verification.spec: Feed the sorted expert-ID list from the bitonic sorter into the pairing stage RTL. Confirm the output sequence pairs experts from opposite ends of the sorted list (index 0 with N-1, 1 with N-2, ...) and forms the pair sequence E_sorted used to feed Algorithm 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Cold experts whose token counts fall below the buffering threshold θ_min are routed to a Token Buffering Router path rather than assigned to compute, as depicted in Figure 8.

verification.spec: In an RTL testbench, drive the scheduler with an expert set where a subset of experts have token counts below theta_min. Confirm those experts are dispatched to the Token Buffering Router output path (not to a compute-die assignment), matching the routing in Figure 8.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler RTL is functionally verified against the reference Algorithm 1 behavior in simulation.

An RTL testbench (or cosimulation harness) has been implemented that drives the scheduler with representative expert activation patterns and checks that the emitted expert-to-chiplet trajectory assignments match those produced by a software model of Algorithm 1.

verification.spec: Implement a Python software model of Algorithm 1. Run the RTL scheduler and the software model on a suite of randomized and hand-crafted expert-activation patterns; check that the emitted expert-to-chiplet trajectory assignments are identical (or equivalent under documented tie-breaking).

sub_tasks.requirements: The RTL simulation reproduces correct idle-chiplet tracking: after an expert e' completes, chiplets not engaged by other running experts are returned to C_idle, matching Algorithm 1 line 15.

verification.spec: In the RTL testbench, simulate an expert e' completing while other experts are still running on some of its trajectory chiplets. Verify that only chiplets not engaged by other running experts become idle in the ICV next cycle, matching Algorithm 1 line 15.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler RTL is synthesized with Synopsys Design Compiler using the UMC 28-nm standard-cell library and characterized for area and latency.
A synthesis flow (scripts/Makefile) has been implemented that invokes Synopsys Design Compiler on the scheduler RTL, targeting the UMC 28-nm technology library used in the paper.

verification.spec: Run the provided synthesis Makefile/scripts and confirm it invokes Synopsys Design Compiler (dc_shell) on the scheduler RTL, using a UMC 28-nm technology library, and terminates producing area/timing reports. Success is a non-zero-area report file for the scheduler top module.

sub_tasks.requirements: The synthesis flow reports post-synthesis area for the complete scheduler (EIT + ICV + E-C Matcher + bitonic sorter and glue logic) in mm^2.

verification.spec: After running the synthesis flow, parse the DC area report and confirm it contains a total area (in mm^2) for the scheduler top module that aggregates the EIT, ICV, E-C Matcher, bitonic sorter, and glue logic sub-modules.

sub_tasks.requirements: The synthesized scheduler total area equals 0.43 mm^2 in UMC 28-nm technology, matching the value reported in Section V-B.

verification.spec: From the Design Compiler area report of the scheduler synthesized in UMC 28-nm, read the total area of the scheduler top module and compare to the paper's reported 0.43 mm^2.

sub_tasks.requirements: The end-to-end scheduling latency (from receiving gating outputs to emitting the expert-to-chiplet assignment) measured in gate-level or post-synthesis timing simulation is sub-microsecond (< 1 μs) under typical expert configurations for the four evaluated MoE models.

verification.spec: Run gate-level or post-synthesis timing simulation of the scheduler with expert-count configurations representative of Phi-3.5-MoE (16), Yuan2.0-M32 (32), DeepSeek-MoE (64), Qwen3-30B-A3B (128). Measure the wall-time from gating-output arrival to the emission of the expert-to-chiplet assignment, and confirm the maximum across configurations is below 1 microsecond.

sub_tasks.requirements: The synthesized scheduler RTL is integrated into the cycle-accurate simulation environment used for the paper's evaluation results.

Code has been implemented so that the RTL-synthesized scheduler's timing and behavior (per-decision latency and outputs) are used to drive the cycle-accurate multi-chiplet simulator that produces the utilization and latency numbers reported in Section VI.

verification.spec: Inspect the cycle-accurate multi-chiplet simulator source and configuration; verify it imports the RTL-synthesized scheduler's per-decision latency (from timing reports) and behavioral model (or cosimulated RTL) rather than using an idealized zero-latency scheduler. Run a short simulation and confirm scheduler-latency stalls appear in the timeline.

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduce isolated single-MoE-layer latency, on-chip memory, and utilization comparisons of FSE-DP versus EP and Hydra across models, datasets, and token-per-iteration settings (16/64/256/1024).
Set up the isolated MoE-layer benchmark harness that runs a single FFN-MoE layer under EP, Hydra, and FSE-DP (with and without paired-load) baselines while excluding attention computation.

Code has been implemented that isolates a single FFN MoE layer for benchmarking, executing only expert compute (gating + expert FFN) without any attention block, to avoid confounding factors from attention implementations.

verification.spec: Locate the isolated MoE-layer benchmark harness. Verify by code inspection that it executes only the gating + expert FFN portion of a single MoE layer (no self-attention block). Run a smoke test and confirm the trace contains no attention operations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that iterates the isolated MoE-layer benchmark across all four models (Phi-3.5-MoE, Yuan2.0-M32, DeepSeek-MoE, Qwen3-30B-A3B) and both language-modeling datasets (Wikitext-2 and C4).

verification.spec: Run the isolated MoE-layer benchmark driver and confirm it iterates over the Cartesian product of {Phi-3.5-MoE, Yuan2.0-M32, DeepSeek-MoE, Qwen3-30B-A3B} × {Wikitext-2, C4}, producing results/logs for all 8 combinations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that sweeps the tokens-per-iteration setting across the four values {16, 64, 256, 1024} for every model/dataset combination in the isolated MoE-layer benchmark.

verification.spec: Run the benchmark driver and confirm that for each (model, dataset) combination it sweeps tokens-per-iteration ∈ {16, 64, 256, 1024}, producing separate result entries for each value.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reports layer latency by averaging over all MoE layers of each network for a given (model, dataset, tokens-per-iteration) configuration.

verification.spec: Inspect the benchmark's reporting code and verify that the reported per-configuration layer latency is computed as the mean across all MoE layers of the network. Cross-check by running the harness in a debug mode that emits per-layer latencies and confirming the reported value equals their mean.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs four scheduling variants in the isolated benchmark: EP baseline, Hydra baseline, FSE-DP without paired-load (A2), and FSE-DP with paired-load (A3), producing comparable latency/memory/utilization numbers.

verification.spec: Invoke the benchmark harness with each of the four scheduling variants (EP, Hydra, FSE-DP w/o paired-load = A2, FSE-DP w/ paired-load = A3) selectable via a flag. Confirm that each variant runs to completion and emits latency, on-chip memory, and utilization metrics in a common format.

sub_tasks.requirements: Token buffering is disabled in the isolated single-layer benchmark (only enabled in the end-to-end evaluation), so each configuration reflects steady-state single-layer behavior only.

verification.spec: Inspect the isolated single-layer benchmark configuration and confirm token-buffering (Algorithm 2) is disabled (e.g., feature flag off or QoS timer forced to zero). Run the benchmark with logging enabled and confirm no token-buffering events occur in the log.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measure and compare single-MoE-layer latency (Figure 9) across all model/dataset/tokens-per-iteration configurations for EP, Hydra, FSE-DP, and FSE-DP+paired-load.
Code has been implemented that logs per-configuration MoE-layer latency in a structured format enabling reproduction of the Figure 9 bar chart (grouped by model, dataset, and tokens-per-iteration).

verification.spec: After running the benchmark, verify that the output file (CSV/JSON) contains per-configuration MoE-layer latency indexed by (model, dataset, tokens_per_iteration, scheduler_variant), sufficient to redraw the Figure 9 bar chart. Load the file and confirm all 8×4×4 = 128 rows are populated.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the majority of (model, dataset, tokens-per-iteration) configurations of the isolated MoE-layer benchmark, FSE-DP (with or without paired-load) achieves the lowest layer latency among EP, Hydra, and FSE-DP variants.

verification.spec: From the benchmark output, for each (model, dataset, tokens_per_iteration) configuration, identify the scheduler with the lowest layer latency. Verify that FSE-DP (either A2 or A3) wins in more than 50% of the configurations.

sub_tasks.requirements: At low tokens-per-iteration (16 and 64), FSE-DP with paired-load yields a measurably lower single-MoE-layer latency than FSE-DP without paired-load, demonstrating the paired-load benefit at small token counts.

verification.spec: From the benchmark output, filter to tokens_per_iteration ∈ {16, 64} across all (model, dataset) combinations. Verify that FSE-DP with paired-load (A3) has strictly lower mean layer latency than FSE-DP without paired-load (A2) in the majority of these low-batch configurations.

sub_tasks.requirements: At higher tokens-per-iteration (256 and 1024), FSE-DP still outperforms EP and Hydra in the isolated MoE-layer latency, with the advantage attributable to fuller D2D-bandwidth utilization rather than paired-load.

verification.spec: From the benchmark output, filter to tokens_per_iteration ∈ {256, 1024}. Verify that FSE-DP (A2 or A3) has lower layer latency than both EP and Hydra in the majority of (model, dataset) combinations, and confirm that A3's paired-load advantage over A2 shrinks in this regime.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hydra shows no obvious latency improvement over EP in the low-batch, high-D2D-bandwidth isolated MoE-layer benchmark, matching the paper's observation that Hydra's token-collective-communication optimization brings limited gains in this regime.

verification.spec: From the benchmark output, compare Hydra vs EP layer latency across all (model, dataset, tokens_per_iteration) configurations in the low-batch, high-D2D-bandwidth setting. Confirm that Hydra's mean speedup over EP is small (e.g., within ±10%) rather than a clear improvement.

sub_tasks.requirements: The overall geometric-mean speedup of FSE-DP over EP and Hydra baselines across the isolated MoE-layer sweeps falls within the reported 1.22x-2.00x range.

verification.spec: Run the isolated MoE-layer sweeps for FSE-DP, EP, and Hydra across all model/dataset/token-count configurations. Compute per-configuration speedup of FSE-DP over each baseline (baseline_latency / FSE-DP_latency), then take the geometric mean. Verify the geomean falls within [1.22, 2.00].

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduce the utilization fluctuation timeline (Figure 11) that compares temporal utilization behavior of EP, Hydra, and FSE-DP within a single MoE layer inference.

verification.spec: Import the simulator module and instantiate an isolated MoE-layer run under each of EP, Hydra, and FSE-DP. Verify the run produces a per-chiplet compute-unit utilization trace with tick-level granularity (a 2D array indexed by chiplet and simulator tick with utilization in [0,1]).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that plots utilization-vs-time curves for the four schemes on the same axes over a matched time window, reproducing the Figure 11 visualization.

verification.spec: Invoke the plotting entry point (e.g., scripts/plot_fig11.py) using traces from all four scheduling schemes, and confirm a single figure is produced with four overlaid utilization-vs-time curves on the same axes over a matched time window.

sub_tasks.requirements: The utilization time series of FSE-DP (with paired-load) exhibits smaller temporal fluctuations (e.g., lower standard deviation / smaller peak-to-valley amplitude) than EP and Hydra across the isolated MoE-layer inference window.

verification.spec: Compute the standard deviation and peak-to-valley amplitude of the utilization time series for FSE-DP-with-paired-load, EP, and Hydra in the Figure 11 setting. Verify std(FSE-DP) < std(EP) and std(FSE-DP) < std(Hydra), and similarly for peak-to-valley amplitude.

sub_tasks.requirements: The mean/steady-state utilization of FSE-DP with paired-load in the Figure 11 setting is higher than that of both EP and Hydra baselines.
